pages.notes: Title: Lecture 24, The control problem for manipulators; instructor/institution; no examinable content.
Contents: control problem; practical considerations (feedforward, dual-rate, lack of knowledge); current industrial systems; Lyapunov stability. Administrative agenda.

Rigid-body equation tau=M(Theta) Theta_ddot+V(Theta,Theta_dot)+G(Theta); M inertia, V Coriolis/centrifugal, G gravity. Right two-link diagram: gray links l1/m1 and l2/m2; downward blue m1g,m2g; red curved joint torques; dashed blue M coupling, green V coupling, red G label. theta1 to horizontal, theta2 to first-link extension.
Adds F(Theta,Theta_dot) for friction and non-rigid-body effects. Partition tau=alpha tau_prime+beta with alpha=M and beta=V+G+F.

tau_prime=qddot_d+Kv Edot+Kp E; E=qd-q. Eddot+Kv Edot+Kp E=0; scalar joint equations require diagonal gains. Diagram puts desired acceleration plus derivative and proportional corrections before M; additive V+G+F after M. Actual position and velocity feedback feed errors and model.

Ideal assumptions: continuous computation, exact model, no sensing/actuation delay; two practical obstacles computation time and model inaccuracy. Load, wear, friction and uncertainty change parameters. Empty outlined lower-right rectangle carries no content.

Sampling: discrete sensor reads and command updates introduce delay, approximation and performance degradation. Slow sampling worsens tracking and can affect stability; faster sampling makes continuous approximation more reasonable, not a stability proof.

Left exact computed-torque diagram maps virtual acceleration through actual-state M and adds actual V+G+F. Right desired position, velocity and acceleration feed dynamic model outside servo; position/velocity errors still feed Kp/Kv torque additions. Written tau=model torque+KpE+KvEdot.

Printed homogeneous Eddot+M^-1 Kv Edot+M^-1 Kp E=0 omits general desired-state feedforward residual. Faster servo, separate model, offline precompute for known trajectory. Nondecoupled M^-1 yields configuration-dependent effective gains; pole language is frozen-configuration, not global time-varying LTI.
Expensive full dynamics need not run at every servo cycle: nonlinear model in slower background process, servo error correction faster. No specified numerical rates.

Red ellipse encloses B(theta)+C(theta) and G(theta), NOT M(theta). B+C receives velocity horizontally and position dashed from below; G receives position. M gets position outside ellipse. Separate B/C formulas are not defined. Text says configuration-space model.

Resisting disturbance tau_d enters arm summing junction with MINUS sign. With E=desired-actual, error forcing is +M^-1 tau_d. Steady error Kp^-1 M^-1 tau_d, order matters. Examples payload, external force, friction change, vibration, unmodeled dynamics. Bottom generic cross-joint claim needs qualification for zero/special coupling.

Hats mean estimated controller model. Actual plant tau=Mqddot+V+G+F; estimated alpha=Mhat beta=Vhat+Ghat+Fhat. Residual Mhat^-1[(M-Mhat) ACTUAL qddot+(V-Vhat)+(G-Ghat)+(F-Fhat)]. Perfect decoupling generally lost; exact matching eliminates residual, but zero sum at one state is not global model identification.

Course description: computation expensive, parameter knowledge incomplete, simpler laws often sufficient. Simple robust separate-joint loops with no full dynamic decoupling, acceptable workspace-wide gains. Robot photograph illustrative, no additional labeled kinematic data.

PID alpha=I beta=0, tau_prime=qddot_d+KvEdot+KpE+Ki integral E. Often desired acceleration set zero because unavailable; diagonal gains and separate joints without model compensation. Diagram P/D/I parallel error paths summed into joint; encoder closes negative feedback. Nonzero acceleration term in literal torque requires inertia scale or normalized convention.

Separate-joint control lacks decoupling, so interactions and imperfect rejection remain. Fixed gains average over postures, not universal critical damping. Adds estimated gravity to PID. Literal acceleration/torque dimensional issue persists; unqualified gravity-causes-steady-error is not true of ideal stable unsaturated integral control.

Energy-like method can establish stability without solving differential equations. Stability is not performance; slow/poor transient can coexist. Informal settling wording needs asymptotic/invariance conditions, not mere nonincrease.

Unforced m xddot+b xdot+kx=0; energy 1/2 m xdot^2+1/2 kx^2; derivative m xdot xddot+kx xdot=-b xdot^2. Rest-position box kx=0 => x=0 requires k nonzero. m,k>0 needed for positive-definite energy; b>0 alone does not prove convergence without invariant-set argument.

General autonomous Xdot=f(X), C1 positive-definite v with v(0)=0; derivative nonpositive for stability, negative away from equilibrium for asymptotic stability. Direct/Second Method names. Intuition says boundedness and pull toward equilibrium too broadly; compact sublevels and stronger convergence conditions must be supplied.

Normalized nonlinear xddot+b(xdot)+k(x)=0; nonlinear damping and spring functions. Strict signs u b(u)>0 for u!=0, x k(x)>0 for x!=0. Candidate 1/2 u^2+integral_0^x k(lambda)dlambda. Reversed negative-x integral gives positive potential; equilibrium/regularity and global compactness need explicit care.

Left correctly differentiates candidate and substitutes xddot+k(x)=-b(xdot), giving -xdot b(xdot)<=0. Right explicitly notes zero derivative at zero velocity need not mean x=0, but then overstates for all trajectories xdot=0 and uses linear -kx rather than nonlinear -k(x). Correct reading restricts to trajectories persisting in zero-dissipation set, yielding xdot=xddot=0 and k(x)=0 => x=0.
Summary of control dynamics, practical considerations, industrial systems and linear/nonlinear Lyapunov applications. No incremental substantive theorem, equation or figure beyond pages729-747.
Reference: Craig (2004), Introduction to robotics: Mechanics and control, 3rd edition, Pearson Prentice Hall. Bibliographic exclusion, not an external-source authorization.
